Confirmed router.js already correctly registers the /projects/:slug/runs/:filename route with the runLogMatch regex (anchored with ^ and $, placed before the :slug catch-all which is also anchored), so no router changes were needed.
All 239 GUI tests pass (16 run-log.test.ts tests + 223 other GUI tests).

comments.note: router.js dispatch() function processes runLogMatch after wpMatch (lines 61-71), but the projectMatch regex is anchored with $ so it correctly does not shadow deeper paths like /runs/:filename. The ordering is logically sound but could be documented with a comment to clarify why the /projects/:slug catch-all is safe despite appearing earlier.

index.html loads all view scripts without type='module', using global-scope IIFE/var patterns. The WP description mentions 'type="module"' as an option but the existing views all use classic scripts — keeping run-log.js as a classic script (no type attribute) is the correct convention match.

summary: Reviewed the single modified file (index.html) and its surrounding context: router.js, run-log.js (WP-007 deliverable), api-client.js, and peer views. The implementation is minimal, correct, and fully idiomatic.

The <script src='/views/run-log.js'></script> tag is positioned at line 43 — after all other view scripts and before app.js. This guarantees renderRunLog is in the global scope when Router.init() dispatches the first hashchange event. Ordering is correct.

Router dispatch order verified: runLogMatch (/^/projects/([^/]+)/runs/([^/]+)$/) is evaluated after projectMatch (/^/projects/([^/]+)$/) which is end-anchored with $. The catch-all cannot shadow the deeper /runs/:filename route. No route shadowing risk.
Router._clearPolling is correctly exposed in the Router module's public API (router.js line 101). The call in run-log.js line 210 is valid and will not throw a ReferenceError.
All five acceptance criteria are confirmed met by code inspection and by the 239-test green suite reported by the Developer.
No duplicate <script> tags found. The script load order is: libs → api-client → theme → router → utils → [views in order] → app. Clean and correct.

comments.note: run-log.js line 135 uses href='#/' for the 'Projects' breadcrumb link, consistent with work-package.js and the project-detail renderProjectDetail view. However, project-detail's renderPlan/renderSynthesis use href='#/projects' instead. The SPA router handles both (/ dispatches renderProjectList, /projects is unmatched and falls to 404). The '#/' form is correct — this pre-existing inconsistency in project-detail.js is outside this WP's scope but worth noting for a future cleanup pass.

router.js dispatch() evaluates projectMatch (the :slug catch-all) before wpMatch and runLogMatch in source order (lines 55-71). This is safe because projectMatch is end-anchored ($), but a brief inline comment — e.g. '// anchored with $ — cannot shadow deeper sub-paths' — would clarify the intent for future maintainers. The Developer's implementation comment already notes this; the Documentation agent should consider adding a comment directly in router.js.
No issues found — code is clean and consistent. The change is a single-line addition to index.html; risk surface is minimal and well-covered by the existing test suite.
